To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

modification of the arginyl residue(s) at the binding site of pigeon liver malic enzyme by arginine-specific reagent(s) phenylglyoxyl or 2, 3-butanediones causes complete and irreversible inactivation of the enzyme.
pigeon liver malic enzyme has an essential arginine residue at the binding sites for malate and dicarboxyliate analogs, and for alpha-hydroxy butyrate.

the arginyl residue(s) modified by phenylglyoaxal or 2.3-butanedone in the pigeon liver malic enzyme are located at or close to the binding site for the dicarboxylyl substrate and its dicarboylic acid analogs and that the dicarboxylate moiety is involved in binding at this site.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a study of the mechanism of pigeon liver malic enzyme and its analogs.
the role of an arginlyl residue in the active site of pigeon liver malic enzyme.
the identification of an essential arginyl residue in pigeon liver malic enzyme, and with the demonstration of its participation in the enzyme-substrate interaction.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
one arginyl residue is essential for catalytic activity and is also involved in the binding site for the substrate dicarboxylate.
the binding site for the dicarboxylate substrates is composed of two arginines, and one of them is essential for activity.
the dicarboxylyl substrate analogs of malate are bound to the enzyme by an arginyl group at the active site.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
arginyl residue 210 is essential for enzyme binding of malate and its dicarbon analogs, and that arginyl residues 210 and 211 are both involved in binding of malate, oxalate, and tartronate.
modification of arginine residues on malic enzyme results in loss of substrate and NADP+ binding sites.
modification by phenylglyoxyal or butanedione results in the loss of two essential arginyl residues on the enzyme, one of which binds the C-1 carbonyl of the substrate.
The main takeaway from our work is that
arginyl residues are involved in binding of the substrate dicarboxylate and that one of these residues is essential for activity.
the binding of dicarboxylicate substrate and NADP+ to pigeon liver malic enzyme is mediated via an arginine residue, and that this arginine is essential for the binding of malate but not of NADP+.
the binding site for dicarboxylytes is a pocket lined by arginyl residues.
